name: Characterization of a 256-pixel NbSi TES bolometer array (CMB, 150 GHz) at ~320 mK with 128:1 SQUID time-domain multiplexing (QUBIC)
plain_name: Characterize an array of ultra-sensitive heat detectors for measuring the Big Bang's afterglow
description: QUBIC TES focal-plane tests: 256 NbSi transition-edge sensors (Tc ~410 mK) cooled to ~320 mK by a He-3 fridge in a pulse-tube cryostat, read out by 128 SQUIDs at 1 K inside a magnetic shield and a cryogenic SiGe ASIC at ~40 K; Tc, I-V, P-T and NEP are measured, with dark-pixel Tc first measured in an Oxford Instruments dilution fridge. The focal plane is 110 mm in diameter.
keywords: Characterize an array of ultra-sensitive heat detectors for measuring the Big Bang's afterglow

sources.citation: M. Piat, G. Stankowiak, E. S. Battistelli et al., 'QUBIC IV: Performance of TES Bolometers and Readout Electronics', arXiv:2101.06787v2 (2021), JCAP 2022

reported_equipment: Oxford Instruments dilution fridge (dark-pixel test bed)

requirements.rationale: The TES bath must reach ~320 mK, below the ~410 mK critical temperature, for the sensors to operate in electro-thermal feedback.
The TES focal plane is 110 mm in diameter and must fit on the sub-K stage.
TES bias and SQUID multiplexer lines run from the cold stages to the warm FPGA readout.
Optional: the SQUID boxes at 1 K are surrounded by a Cryophy magnetic shield; a test cryostat needs equivalent shielding for the SQUIDs.
Optional: dark-pixel critical temperature (~412 mK) is mapped by slowly raising the temperature through the transition, so the stage must regulate around 412 mK.
Optional: the QUBIC cryostat is pulse-tube cooled (dry); pulse-tube microphonics were the dominant excess noise.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
